subsystems.name: Agent layer
subsystems.role: each vehicle, driver or delivery slot runs a software agent that senses its state and makes local decisions.

subsystems.name: Communication mesh
subsystems.role: lets agents exchange offers and updates without a central server.

subsystems.name: Negotiation and auction engine
subsystems.role: agents bid for delivery windows, routes and loads, resolving conflicts by agreed rules.

subsystems.name: Multi-agent learning system
subsystems.role: trains agent policies to improve global fleet efficiency over time.

subsystems.name: Simulation and digital twin
subsystems.role: a safe, fast environment to train and test before real-world deployment.

subsystems.name: Integration layer
subsystems.role: connects the mesh to existing order management, telematics and mapping systems.

buildSteps.title: Define objectives and constraints
buildSteps.detail: set clear goals (e.g. minimise empty kilometres, meet time windows) and hard constraints (driver hours, vehicle capacity).

buildSteps.title: Build the simulation
buildSteps.detail: create a digital twin of the fleet, roads and demand, using real historical data where available.

buildSteps.title: Design agent architecture
buildSteps.detail: decide what each agent senses, what it controls, and how it communicates; choose between fully decentralised and hybrid designs.

buildSteps.title: Implement negotiation rules
buildSteps.detail: code the bidding, acceptance and conflict-resolution protocols so agents can reach agreements quickly.

buildSteps.title: Train the learning system
buildSteps.detail: run multi-agent reinforcement learning in simulation, shaping rewards so individual incentives align with fleet-wide efficiency.

buildSteps.title: Validate in simulation
buildSteps.detail: test on held-out scenarios, stress-test with disruptions (road closures, demand spikes), and check safety and fairness.

buildSteps.title: Pilot on a limited real route
buildSteps.detail: deploy on a small number of vehicles with human oversight, comparing performance to the existing centralised scheduler.

buildSteps.title: Scale and harden
buildSteps.detail: expand coverage, add fail-safes for communication loss, and integrate with legacy systems.

buildSteps.title: Operate and update
buildSteps.detail: continuously retrain and monitor for drift, ensuring the mesh remains robust and fair.

prerequisites.why: algorithms can learn cooperative behaviour in simulation, but transferring to noisy real-world logistics is not yet reliable.
GPS, cellular and satellite links already report location and status at second-scale intervals.
small computers can run decision policies locally without waiting for a central server.
academic standards exist (e.g. contract net), but industry-wide adoption in logistics is limited.
simulators exist for traffic and warehouses, but open, multi-company fleet simulations are rare.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes and single-company pilots (e.g. warehouse robots, last-mile delivery)
pathway.unlocks: proof that decentralised agents can beat centralised dispatch on narrow tasks.

pathway.milestone: hybrid systems where a central planner sets goals and agents negotiate locally
pathway.unlocks: gradual adoption without replacing existing fleet software.
load sharing and fewer empty runs across carriers.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous mesh spanning many carriers, with dynamic pricing and real-time replanning
pathway.unlocks: system-wide efficiency gains and resilience to disruptions.
